liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments were stable at {{cash_like@FY2025}}, a change of {{cash_like.change@FY2025}}, giving cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.

Debt due within one year rose by {{debt_due_1y.change@FY2025}} to {{debt_due_1y@FY2025}}, while borrowings due within two years fell by {{borrowings_due_2y.change@FY2025}} to {{borrowings_due_2y@FY2025}}, so cash on hand covers the near-term maturities without new funding.

Free cash flow after lease payments turned positive at {{fcf_after_leases@FY2025}}, from {{fcf_after_leases@FY2024}} in FY2024, taking FCF after leases to debt up by {{fcf_after_leases_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_after_leases_to_debt@FY2025}}.

Customer prepayments rose, with contract liabilities up by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}} and advance ticket cover at {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}, the lowest of the peer group.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Cash generation: FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}}, the weakest of the group ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2025}}), with capex intensity at {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Maturities: debt due within one year rose by {{debt_due_1y.change@FY2025}} to {{debt_due_1y@FY2025}}, and cash flow after leases covers only {{fcf_after_leases_to_debt@FY2025}} of debt, so refinancing depends on access to the bond market, where the group placed senior unsecured bonds under its EMTN programme.
Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}, so a larger part of the cash balance is customers' prepayments.
